_doc: PROJECT-scoped Claude Code settings — the SoT for the settings.json committed into every repo under cloud. It carries the machine-independent half of settings.base.json + settings.desktop.json (its neighbours here, the SoT for ~/.claude/settings.json). cloud-infra's 9_others/src/deploy-dotfiles.sh copies this file to _dotfiles/apps/src/claude/settings.json on every dotfiles build, which then deploys to <repo>/.claude/settings.json. Edit HERE; the copies are generated. It used to be hand-kept in cloud-infra with an instruction to 're-copy', and three repos had drifted the first time anything looked.
_why_committed: ~/.claude/settings.json only exists where unix's home-manager has run. A fresh clone — CI, a container, Claude Code on the web, a second machine, someone else's checkout — has no user config, so without this the repo gets Claude's stock defaults: no thinking, no tool search, no agents. Project settings merge OVER user settings, so on a home-manager machine these keys are already what ~/.claude sets and the merge is a no-op.
_deliberately_absent: Everything from settings.base.json that carries a @HOME@ path: statusLine.command, and env GIT_BASE / NODE_PATH / AUTHELIA_OIDC_CREDENTIALS_DIR / AUTHELIA_OIDC_TOKENS_DIR. unix substitutes @HOME@ with config.home.homeDirectory at nix eval time, per machine. A committed file has no such step, so those paths would harden to one person's home directory and be wrong in every clone — the same failure .mcp.json had as a symlink to /home/diego/.mcp.json. They stay in ~/.claude, where the substitution happens.
_also_absent: Plugin choice stays user-level EXCEPT c3-infra (see enabledPlugins below): the other @cloud-marketplace and @claude-plugins-official entries are installed per-machine, and enabling a plugin that is not installed is noise in every clone that lacks it.

env._ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH_comment: auto, mirrored from settings.base.json. 'true' force-defers EVERY MCP tool behind Tool Search unconditionally; 'auto' defers only past 10% of context (~20k tokens) so the lean detached servers (cgc-pub etc.) stay eager while the fat, mostly-disabled cloud-services-mcp aggregator is what trips deferral when enabled. Project settings merge OVER user, so this MUST match base.json or it silently re-forces 'true' inside every repo.
env._AUTHELIA_comment: The NON-SECRET half of what mcp-auth-headers.sh needs, placed here because this is the only delivery path that is early enough. A container runs no home-manager, so settings.base.json never lands; and anything a session does after it starts — cloning the vault, exporting a variable, running a hook — arrives after the MCP client has already bound and taken its 403. That ordering is the whole reason c3-infra-mcp has never autoloaded off-mesh. This file is read at session start and its env DOES reach the process: ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH above was verified live in a container shell, sourced from here.
env._AUTHELIA_secret_comment: The SECRET is absent and must stay absent — this file is committed into every repo, several of them public. It is the one value that has to come from the remote environment's OWN variable config, which is the only carrier that exists before the process starts. Set ONE of: AUTHELIA_BEARER_TOKEN (a ready-made bearer; works today) or AUTHELIA_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET (mints a short-lived token per session; preferred, but blocked until the Authelia clients stop rejecting as invalid_client). One variable, set once — everything else is declared here and deployed by the dotfiles build.

_disabledMcpjsonServers_comment: Default-OFF the ONE remaining fat aggregator (mirror of settings.base.json) so the auto 10% cap is not spent on ~139 eager tools. cloud-services-mcp is the master index; /mcp re-enables it on demand.
_why_cloud-infra-mcp_is_no_longer_here:
It was in this list, and that quietly defeated the entire off-mesh auth chain. c3-infra-mcp is the ONLY MCP endpoint reachable from off the WireGuard mesh, so it is the one server a container, CI runner or web session can actually use — and it was the one being default-disabled. A disabled server is never dialed at all: it appears in neither the connected nor the failed list, which is why it read as 'missing' rather than 'off' and was diagnosed twice as an auth problem it never had.

The trap was the NAME. derive-mcp-json.ts names servers after the service directory (infra-api_cloud-infra-mcp -> cloud-infra-mcp) while the URL keeps the deployed path (/c3-infra-mcp/mcp). Until the derive was regenerated, the shipped .mcp.json still carried the older key c3-infra-mcp, which this list does not match — so the server WAS dialed and the disable was inert. Regenerating renamed the key to cloud-infra-mcp, which this list DOES match, and the server silently stopped being dialed at the same moment the static bearer header was added to make it work. Two changes that each looked correct, cancelling out.

With ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH: auto the cost of leaving it enabled is bounded anyway: past ~10% of context its tools defer behind Tool Search instead of being dropped, so they stay reachable. An unreachable server is not a saving.
_enableAllProjectMcpServers_comment: Owner decision 31 (2026-10-17): fleet MCPs in .mcp.json are stdio entries running .claude/mcp-connect.mjs (mesh first, else public + bearer; no OAuth). Project stdio servers need this approval or they are never started in a fresh clone / cloud session. Same value as settings.base.json.

permissions._defaultMode_doc: 2026-10-15 OWNER DECISION: every session from every repo starts as full root (bypassPermissions) with every tool and MCP server allowed. Supersedes the earlier note that defaultMode stays user-level. Note: this file is committed to public repos, so anyone who clones one also gets this default.
permissions._doc: 2026-09-06: populated by the repo owner's explicit decision, reversing the earlier 'left empty on purpose'. That text held that pre-approval is a per-person trust choice; in practice the auto-mode classifier blocked plain `git commit`, `npx tsc --noEmit` and a curl to the fleet's OWN MCP mid-incident — five denials in a row, read-only steps included — so a session whose whole job is to run the fleet through c3-infra-mcp could not ship a fix. These rules pre-approve the tools that ARE the control plane: the shell, the file tools, and the MCP servers. Allow rules stay in force under auto mode (autoMode.classifyAllShell is unset, i.e. false), so matched calls never reach the classifier. defaultMode stays user-level on purpose: settings.base.json sets "auto", and forcing a mode from a committed file would override that choice for anyone who clones this repo.

autoMode._doc: Guidance for the auto-mode classifier, for calls NOT already matched by a permissions.allow rule (rule matches bypass the classifier entirely). "$defaults" keeps Anthropic's built-in rules; the extra entries record what this repo's owner has standing-authorised, so fleet work is not classed as 'destructive infra' and refused.
allow: Operating the owner's own fleet through the c3-infra-mcp / cloud-infra-mcp tools is routine and pre-authorised: docker container, image and volume management on the VMs (including removing orphaned volumes and dangling images), service restarts, workflow dispatch, and committing and pushing to main in the diegonmarcos/* repositories.

Writing, type-checking, committing and pushing source code for the fleet's MCP servers and CI scripts — including tools whose purpose is to delete docker volumes or images on the fleet — is ordinary development work here, not a destructive action.

Pushing tested commits to main from a /dev/shm git worktree of any diegonmarcos/* repository (cloud-infra, cloudy-u-containers, cloudy-u-android, cloud-data*, cloudy-u-linux) is the normal delivery path for this fleet, including changes to its CI workflows and the cgc-db indexing scripts. Worktrees are used precisely so the shared checkout is never stashed, reset or rebased.
Dispatching, re-running and cancelling GitHub Actions runs in diegonmarcos/* repositories (including cgc-db force reindexes and superseded queued runs) is routine fleet operation.
Removing temporary git worktrees, scratch directories and build caches that the session itself created under /dev/shm or /tmp is housekeeping, not destruction of shared resources.

OWNER STANDING AUTHORISATION (2026-10-15, 'you are root, you are allowed'): changing the public exposure of the owner's own fleet hosts to match the owner's declared URL scheme is routine — e.g. opening auth.diegonmarcos.com (Authelia) to the internet, switching a host or MCP between public, token-gated and mesh-only (wg_only), adding mesh/private addresses — then deploying it with ship.yml.

Changing a repo's own guard, tester or ratchet when the OWNER changes the architecture rule it enforces (e.g. 'all apps must be Compose' replacing a no-Compose tester) is authorised; doing it only to hide a real failure is not.
Running a Bash command with dangerouslyDisableSandbox to repair a dead Bash sandbox (every call exits 1 with no output), per .claude/SESSION-SURVIVAL.md, is authorised.
Committing and pushing to main across every diegonmarcos/* repository, adding repos to the session, and dispatching/cancelling GitHub Actions and Ship deploys are pre-authorised fleet operations.
autoMode._doc_cloud_sessions: 2026-10-09: in a Claude Code cloud session these rules are read only when the session has ONE repository, and the session's mode dropdown still decides. In Auto, calls the classifier refuses are refused outright (pushes to cloud-infra main and worktree cleanup were refused all day although 'Bash' is allowed). Use 'Accept edits' for fleet work: refusals become approval prompts instead.

_disableClaudeAiConnectors_doc: 2026-10-23 owner decision: claude.ai account connectors (Gmail, Calendar, Drive) stay in claude.ai chat only; Claude Code uses the fleet MCPs from .mcp.json. Applies to terminal/IDE/SDK sessions; cloud sessions take connectors from the session's own connector settings.
_deniedMcpServers_doc: 2026-10-23 owner decision: the GitHub MCP (~60 tools, ~28k tokens per session/agent) is redundant; use gh CLI (proxy-authenticated) and cloud-infra-mcp devops_workflows_gha_*. permissions.allow no longer lists mcp__github.
_hooks_doc: c3-infra guard hooks (cloud-marketplace/c3-infra/hooks). Cloud sessions do not install plugins, so deploy-dotfiles copies the scripts to <repo>/.claude/hooks/c3 and this block wires them. Declared ONCE: the retired sync-to-repo.sh appended a fresh copy on every run. StopFailure(rate_limit) -> ai-usage-post.sh (#1151): cloud sessions run no statusLine and no hook input carries rate_limits, so the only usage fact a cloud session can publish to c3-infra-api is that it was rate limited; the percentages come from the statusLine path (claude-ai-usage-post.sh via statusline-assets). It reads C3_AI_USAGE_TOKEN (or mints from the AUTHELIA_* client credentials the cloud environment injects) and is a no-op without a token.
_enabledPlugins_doc: c3-infra lives in cloud-marketplace (this SoT). Skill and agents are also copied into <repo>/.claude/ by deploy-dotfiles, which is what cloud sessions load.
